title: The manifest walk spends ~85% of its CPU building pathlib objects, on every machine, every 300 s
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/manifest.py:186-226 (`Path(file_path).relative_to(project_dir)` and `rel.parts` per video file, `size_fn=os.path.getsize`), :369-373 (300 s loop)
what: For every video file the walk builds a `Path`, calls `relative_to` (which itself builds and compares several `Path`s), then `rel.parts` and `rel.as_posix()`, and stats the file a second time with `os.path.getsize`. The pathlib work, not the disk, is the cost. It runs whether or not a project is selected (rollup-only projects pay it too), on the manifest thread, holding the GIL against the tray, the reporter and the lanes.
cost: 50k files: 3.6 s of pure-Python CPU every 300 s on a local NVMe tree (1.2% of a core, all day, beside Resolve). At commercial scale (64 projects, 500k files on a base or wired rig) about 36 s per pass, 12% of a core, before any SMB latency. The second stat per file is a network round trip on an SMB `local_root`.
evidence: cProfile of one scan: 9.4 s profiled total, of which `pathlib.relative_to` 5.8 s cumulative (38,293 calls, 783k `PurePath.__getitem__`, 898k `Path.__init__`), `os.stat` via getsize 1.8 s. A rewrite with `os.scandir` recursion, a carried `"prefix/"` string, a carried in-Proxy flag and `DirEntry.stat()` (free on Windows) produced identical rollups for all 10 projects in 0.47 s best of 3 against 3.58 s (7.6x).
ledger: related to PL-RES-107 / prac-perf-3 (open: base rig walks the NAS, extra getsize). New here: the dominant cost is pathlib and it hits every machine, so the recorded fix (scandir + `entry.stat()`) alone leaves most of it in place.
fix: Walk with an explicit `os.scandir` stack carrying the relative prefix as a string and an `in_proxy` flag; size from `entry.stat().st_size`; `VIDEO_EXTS` as a frozenset. Must keep: the conflict-marker count ahead of the extension filter, the NFC fold only for comparison, the bytes-on-disk rel that is returned, the present-before-and-after check in `refresh_once`, and `size_fn` as a test seam (make `entry.stat` the default and accept an override).
risk: low risk (output pinned by the existing manifest tests; the probe shows equal rollups).

title: An unchanged manifest is still re-sent in full every 10 minutes, and one changed project re-sends all of them
what: Suppression is all-or-nothing per section: `local_manifest` is one sha1, so a new file in one ticked project re-sends every ticked project's per-file lists, and the server DELETEs and re-INSERTs all of them. And even with nothing changed, the forced 600 s resend ships the whole section again so the server can re-learn what it already holds.
cost: An editor with 10 ticked projects of ~5k files: the heavy body is 3.55 MB (measured) and the server rewrites ~40k `editor_media` rows, 0.27 s of write locks on desktop NVMe (27 ms per project; a NAS is slower). Idle, that is 144 resends a day: about 510 MB a day of upload per machine and ~5.8M row writes a day, every one of them a no-op. At 20 machines: ~10 GB/day into the dashboard and ~115M no-op row writes/day, all retained by the hourly ZFS snapshots (res-time-scale-10). While one project is syncing, the 300 s rescan changes the section and the other nine are rewritten with it.
evidence: `probe_manifest.py` (3.55 MB body for 10 selected projects, 16.8 MB for 64); `probe_server_write.py` (10 x 4,000-row `replace_editor_media` = 0.27 s, WAL grew 4.7 MB); code read of `_drop_unchanged_sections` (`(now - sent[1]) >= SECTION_RESEND_SECONDS` re-sends regardless of digest).
ledger: related to CR-62 (open: "the per-project change signal"), res-time-scale-10 and PL-RES-44 (open, gzip). The quantified cost of the forced resend and the keep-alive alternative below are new.
fix: Keep digests per project key (and per media-tree project), send only the changed keys (the server already treats an absent key as "leave it alone"). Replace the forced full resend with a keep-alive: send `{rel: digest}` for unchanged projects; the server bumps `refreshed_at` / `reported_at` with one UPDATE when its stored digest matches and answers `resend: [rels]` when it does not (restored backup, pruned rows, truncation). Must keep: the 14-day age-out still sees live machines (the keep-alive touches the timestamps), a failed POST suppresses nothing, a new editor identity clears the state.
effort: M effort (both sides of the wire, additive field, dashboard first)

title: Once `_fit_payload` has trimmed the manifest, it is never suppressed again: rebuilt, shed and re-sent every heavy tick, with a WARNING every minute
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/reporter.py:1177-1183 (compares the digest of the UNFITTED section), :1199-1206 (`_note_sections_sent` stores the digest of the FITTED section), :1259-1262 (the WARNING)
what: `_drop_unchanged_sections` runs before fitting and hashes the full manifest; `_note_sections_sent` runs after the POST and hashes the trimmed one. When the body is over budget the two never match, so the unchanged-section suppression (CR-62, ops-efficiency-1) is permanently off for exactly the machines with the biggest manifests. Fitting is deterministic, so the same input always yields the same trimmed output; nothing is gained by re-sending it.
cost: An editor with 30 ticked projects of >=2,000 files (8.5 MB untrimmed): every 60 s the reporter serialises ~8.5-18 MB twice (digest, then fit), trims, sends, and logs `report payload is 8.5 MB (budget 7.3 MB): dropped the per-file lists ...` at WARNING. 60-140 ms of CPU and a transient multi-MB string per minute, 1,440 identical WARNING lines a day pushing the useful lines out of the rotated `companion.log` a support session reads, and 30-64 `editor_media_project` upserts a minute on the dashboard instead of one round every 10 minutes.
evidence: `probe_suppress.py`: three heavy posts of an unchanged manifest. 10 projects (2.8 MB, under budget): sent, omitted, omitted (CPU 58, 11, 11 ms). 30 projects: sent, sent, sent, each 4,925 bytes after trimming, CPU 82, 60, 61 ms, WARNING each time. 64 projects: sent x3, 141, 141, 137 ms.
ledger: new (a hole in CR-62's fix; KNOWN_BUGS states the fitted digest is recorded on purpose but not this consequence).
fix: Record both digests on acceptance (`(unfitted, fitted, at)`) and suppress when the new unfitted digest equals the stored unfitted one; keep the fitted one only for the "shed means not sent" rule. Log the budget WARNING on a change of the shed set, DEBUG otherwise. Must keep: a shed section still counts as not sent; a server-truncated reply still clears the state.

title: One byte over the budget strips the per-file lists from EVERY ticked project, not just enough of them
what: Step 1 sets `originals`/`proxies` to None on every project in one go and only then re-measures. The manifest is already in priority order (ticked, then most recently touched), so dropping lists from the tail until the body fits would keep the file lists of the projects that matter. Instead a machine that crosses 7 MiB by one project loses all of its per-file presence at once.
cost: An editor ticks a 26th project of >=2,000 files (body ~7.4 MB). From the next heavy report every project goes rollup-only. On the dashboard, `replace_editor_media` is no longer called for any of them, so their `editor_media` rows freeze at the last full report and are deleted by the 14-day age-out (db.py:10807-10809), after which the per-file sync view for that machine has nothing for any project, not just the new one. The editor did nothing but tick one more project.
evidence: `probe_suppress.py`: 30 projects at 8.5 MB -> `dropped the per-file lists from 30 project(s)`, final body 4,925 bytes against a 7.3 MB budget (99.9% of the budget unused). Dashboard path read at api.py:11388-11391 (lists only replaced when not None).
ledger: new; related to res-time-scale-4 (open, per-project 2000-file cap) and B6.
fix: In step 1 drop lists from the lowest-priority projects first (iterate the manifest in reverse order, re-measure every few projects or by subtracting each project's encoded size), stopping as soon as the body fits. Must keep: copies, never in-place edits of the cache's dicts; `truncated: True` on every project that lost its list; the later shedding steps unchanged.

title: A changed heavy section is serialised three times per report
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/reporter.py:360-371 (`_section_digest`, sort_keys), :1177 (digest before fitting), :1236 (`_fit_payload` encode), :1202 (digest again after the POST)
what: Each heavy tick with a changed manifest JSON-encodes it once with `sort_keys` to digest it, once to measure and send it, and once more with `sort_keys` to record what was accepted. When nothing was trimmed the third digest is identical to the first. And on every idle heavy tick (60 s) the unchanged manifest is still re-encoded once just to discover it is unchanged, although `ManifestCache` knows whether it rescanned.
cost: 10 projects: 8 + 11 + 8 ms; 64 projects: 59 + 55 + 59 ms plus transient copies of a 16 MB string; the idle digest is 8-59 ms a minute per machine. Small, but it is on the reporter thread on the base rig, which also runs the encoder and the indexer.
evidence: `probe_manifest.py` timings (encode 11 / 55 ms, digest 8 / 59 ms for 10 / 64 projects).
ledger: new (COMP-CORE-5 of 2026-08-14 removed the fourth serialisation; these three remain).
fix: Reuse the pre-fit digest in `_note_sections_sent` when the section came through `_fit_payload` untouched; give `ManifestCache` (and the media-tree cache) a generation counter so an unchanged generation skips the digest entirely. Must keep: digest of the fitted content when it was trimmed (or the two-digest rule of comp-core-3).

title: On macOS the idle probe spawns `ioreg` on every report tick, uncached
confidence: PLAUSIBLE (not measurable on this Windows rig)
where: companion/src/ccsync_companion/idle.py:213-260 (`default_ioreg_run`, no cache); capabilities.py:317 and :383 (`idle_seconds` recomputed on every build, cached assembly or not); app.py:2396 / 2485 / 7639 (the same probe handed to the jobs runner and ingest)
what: `capabilities.build` deliberately re-reads `idle_seconds` on every report, and on a Mac each read is a `/usr/sbin/ioreg -c IOHIDSystem -d 1 -w 0` subprocess. The report runs every 5 s while any lane is syncing and every 60 s otherwise; the jobs runner and ingest ask the same probe on their own cadence.
cost: Estimated 10-30 ms per spawn (fork/exec plus an IOKit dump): ~17,000 spawns a day on a Mac during an all-day upload, ~1,440 idle. Small on its own, but it is a process spawn every 5 s on a laptop on battery, for a number whose resolution the scheduler needs only to the minute (the idle floor is 60-300 s).
evidence: code read; no cache in `MacIdleProbe.seconds_idle` or `default_ioreg_run`. Windows uses `GetLastInputInfo` (no spawn) and is unaffected.
fix: Cache the ioreg answer for ~5 s and extrapolate (`cached + (now - cached_at)`; any input resets it on the next real read). Must keep: None still means "cannot tell, so NOT idle" on both sides; a cached value never claims more idleness than real time allows.
